question: The lengths of the three sides of a triangle are given as 3 cm, 4 cm and 5 cm. The ratio of their corresponding altitudes to the opposite vertices will be:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The ratio of altitudes of a triangle is always inversely proportional to the ratio of their corresponding sides.

Ratio of the given sides = 3 ∶ 4 ∶ 5

Ratio of their corresponding altitudes = 1/3 ∶ 1/4 ∶ 1/5

Multiplying by the LCM of (3, 4, 5) which is 60:

Ratio of altitudes = 20 ∶ 15 ∶ 12

**∴ The correct answer is 20 ∶ 15 ∶ 12.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/08e493ceb26d1cecf5ff24815ed689421e4dec774f95a6a6ae86e796bc93045a.png] 

**Given:**

Sides of the triangle, a = 3 cm, b = 4 cm, and c = 5 cm.

**Formula Used:**

Area of a triangle = 1/2 × base × height

**Calculation:**

⇒ Let the corresponding altitudes to the given sides be h₁, h₂, and h₃.

⇒ Since 3² + 4² = 5², the given sides form a right-angled triangle.

⇒ Area of the triangle = 1/2 × 3 × 4 = 6 cm²

⇒ Altitude corresponding to side 3 cm: 1/2 × 3 × h₁ = 6 ⇒ h₁ = 4 cm

⇒ Altitude corresponding to side 4 cm: 1/2 × 4 × h₂ = 6 ⇒ h₂ = 3 cm

⇒ Altitude corresponding to side 5 cm: 1/2 × 5 × h₃ = 6 ⇒ h₃ = 12/5 = 2.4 cm

⇒ Ratio of altitudes = h₁ ∶ h₂ ∶ h₃ = 4 ∶ 3 ∶ 2.4

⇒ Multiply the ratio by 10 to remove the decimal: 40 ∶ 30 ∶ 24

⇒ Divide the terms by 2 to get the simplest integer form: 20 ∶ 15 ∶ 12

**∴ The correct answer is 20 ∶ 15 ∶ 12.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relation Between Sides and Altitudes

Since the area of a given triangle is constant, an altitude is strictly inversely proportional to its corresponding base length. Therefore, a × hₐ = b × hb = c × h꜀.

Heron's Formula

The area of any scalene triangle can also be calculated universally using its side lengths: Area = √[s(s−a)(s−b)(s−c)], where s is the semi-perimeter given by (a+b+c)/2.

Pythagorean Triplet

A set of three positive integers that satisfy a² + b² = c² is known as a Pythagorean triplet. A triangle constructed with these specific side lengths is always right-angled at the vertex opposite to the longest side.
